solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shady group of men stealing pounds

indicators.note: a thief takes something and holds it, so the group closes round the money

parts.note: a military unit is a body of soldiers
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shady gang of crooks makes off with some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: UNIT takes in L: UN(L)IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlit place is dark and in shadow, so shady in the literal sense of lacking light.

clue.text: Adding padding to English operas, following leading composer

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the last-named pieces go first

parts.note: up means ahead, as in a goal up
Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets
E, abbreviation for English
Wagner's Ring is a cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: Someone padding out English operas after the example of a great composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading composer' reads as one phrase, but leading is UP on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstering is fitting furniture with padding, springs and covers, so it means adding padding to it.

clue.text: Lakes surrounding isle with cooler shade

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the lakes enclose the isle

parts.note: L for lake, twice
I, abbreviation for island or isle
AC, air conditioning, something that cools

explanation.surface: Lakes around an island, cooler in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: L(I)L + AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple colour, so it is a shade in the colour sense.

clue.text: Trouble with learner breaking wrecked car part

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: wrecked and tight are both slang for drunk
to ail is to trouble
L, the learner plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver crashes and damages part of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrecked' suggests a crash, but it means drunk. T(AIL L)IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail light is the red lamp at the back of a vehicle, one part of a car.

clue.text: Case after case of Soave having a soothing effect

indicators.note: tells the solver the first-named piece is placed later than the second
the case of a word is its outside, so only its two end letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Soave
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A wine buyer orders crate after crate of the Italian white Soave, finding it relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is grammatical, not a crate; Soave is an Italian white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative drug calms and relaxes, so the adjective describes anything with a calming, soothing influence.

clue.text: Lashing out, striking husband making gesture

indicators.note: out means disordered, as when things are out of place
striking here means striking out, crossing a letter off

parts.note: taken as written
H, abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An angry spouse lashes out and hits her husband, making a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H from LASHING and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a gesture or sign conveying a message, such as a wave of the hand.

clue.text: Comedy turn by European? Catching it is boring

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: dry means dull, boring
a roll is a turn, as of a ship or a body
E, abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European comedian's turn is found boring by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for the turn by European, which DRY catches: D(ROLL E)RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is quaint humour or jesting, a word for comedy or amusing behaviour.

clue.text: Was a lush plant raised by newsroom chief?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: to plant is to pot, put into a pot
ED, editor, head of a newsroom

explanation.surface: A lush plant grown by a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for leafy growth; it is a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink heavily, and a lush is a heavy drinker, so toped means acted as one.

clue.text: Trash from museum is filling luggage on vacation

parts.note: the V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of luggage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stuff from a museum fills a suitcase while its owner is away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: V AND A + L(IS)E. 'Trash' is the verb, to wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash a place is to wreck it deliberately, which is to vandalise it.

clue.text: Controlling business, what good person's doing for Scot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a firm that owns controlling shares in other firms

definitions.text: what good person's doing for Scot
definitions.meaning: second, cryptic meaning: a good person is ST (saint), and to make SCOT, ST must hold CO, the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A boardroom question about a dominant firm, then a riddle about how a decent soul treats a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the crossword saint, CO is company; SCOT is S(CO)T, ST holding CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A holding company exists to own and control subsidiary firms rather than trade itself.

clue.text: Struggle to suppress urge about food served up — it may be in a bun

definitions.text: it may be in a bun

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and keep in

parts.note: to vie is to compete, struggle
to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, concerning
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Someone fights the urge to eat food that is served in a bun.
explanation.walkthrough: V(EGG)IE, then RE GRUB turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie burger is a meatless patty, usually served in a bread bun like any burger.

clue.text: I'm amused about state doubling use of phone

indicators.note: about means going round, so the laughter abbreviation is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, the text message for amusement

indicators.note: doubling means the same state abbreviation is written twice in a row

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California
the same state again

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a state that has twice the phone usage.
explanation.walkthrough: LO(CAL CAL)L.
explanation.definitionFit: A local call is a phone call within the same area, one particular use of the telephone.

clue.text: One might make quack medic rankle periodically

parts.note: DR, doctor

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of rankle

explanation.surface: A fake doctor's antics irritate the real medic now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' suggests a fraudulent doctor, but here it is the noise a duck makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, and ducks quack, so it is a bird that might produce that call.

clue.text: Land splits at that tropical island

indicators.note: a word that splits another breaks into its middle and sits inside

parts.note: 'at that' means also, in addition, as in 'and a good one at that'
to land a fish is to bag it, catch it

explanation.surface: A country is divided at that point near an island in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a country, but it is the verb to catch. TO(BAG)O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, the smaller partner of Trinidad in one nation.

clue.text: Leader of batsmen with runs smashed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of batsmen
laddered tights have runs in them

explanation.surface: A cricket captain piles on runs and his side smashes the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' and 'batsmen' suggest cricket, but runs here are ladders in tights. Bladdered is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed and bladdered are both informal British words for very drunk.

clue.text: Great solvers are doing this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, informal British praise
second meaning: what you do to a puzzle or code when you solve it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue flatters the reader; in British slang 'cracking' means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it is informal praise for something excellent; as a verb form it describes working out a puzzle.

clue.text: Crowd of one hundred playing golf, maybe

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100
on means performing, being played
a golf course; 'maybe' signals an example

explanation.surface: A crowd of a hundred plays a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering of people, a throng or crowd, as well as an open hall.

clue.text: See painter framing pleasant flowering plant

indicators.note: framing means bordering on all sides, so the outer pieces go round the inner one

parts.note: lo, as in lo and behold
nice means pleasant
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Look at an artist framing a pretty picture of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: LO and RA frame NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonicera is the botanical genus of honeysuckles, flowering shrubs and climbers.

clue.text: Conservatism of troops before battle

indicators.note: before tells the solver the first piece comes ahead of the second in the word

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
action is military combat

explanation.surface: Soldiers stick to the old ways right before going into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Political reaction is opposition to change and a wish to return to older ways, a hardline form of conservatism.

clue.text: Queen touring old wing of palace, perhaps

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the queen's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Queen Anne, British monarch
ex- means former

explanation.surface: A queen is shown round the old wing of a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: ANN(EX)E.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension added to a building, and a palace wing is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Effect of smoking: positive experiences at first

indicators.note: at first means placed at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: ups, as in ups and downs
smoking hot, very hot

explanation.surface: A survey of how smoking feels good at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final result or outcome of something, its effect.

clue.text: Some miner I'd antagonised around the pits

indicators.note: turned around means read from right to left
some means only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: a run of letters across miner I'd an(tagonised)

explanation.surface: A miner has upset someone working down the pits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' looks like a coal mine, matching the miner, but it means the lowest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, and 'the pits' is slang for the very worst.

clue.text: How rave begins, playing party music

indicators.note: how a word begins is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of rave
on means being played
a do is a party

explanation.surface: How a rave starts: a party with music playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting sections.

clue.text: Rogue put on concert introduced by this person's composition

indicators.note: something rogue has gone off course and out of order
introduced by means preceded by, so the last piece named comes first

parts.note: 'this person is', from the setter's view: I'm
a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
the letters of put rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue performer puts on a concert featuring the setter's own piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' is the setter speaking of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is a short piece of music, often for piano, written as if improvised.

clue.text: Old poem found under page eleven or thirteen?

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed lower, so it follows the other piece

parts.note: P, abbreviation for page
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: An old poem appears at the foot of page eleven or thirteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like page numbers, but they are examples of a kind of number.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven and thirteen are prime numbers, divisible only by one and themselves; the question mark signals examples.

clue.text: The one preparing to imprison dissolute chancer

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock someone inside, so one piece goes round the other
dissolute means loose-living, so the letters are in a loose, disordered arrangement

parts.note: the letters of chancer rearranged
priming is getting something ready

explanation.surface: Someone who is the one getting ready to lock up a disreputable opportunist.
explanation.walkthrough: PRI(NCECHAR)MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Charming is the ideal suitor of fairy tales, so 'the one' a romantic is waiting for.

clue.text: After cutting back, champion swallows a liqueur

indicators.note: to swallow is to take something inside
once the back end is cut off, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to champion a cause is to advocate it; an advocate is a champion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the pruning is done, a winner downs a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVOCATE loses its E, then takes in A: ADVOCA(A)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs, sugar and brandy.

clue.text: Poet's always including the writer's title

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A poet always puts his own name in the title.
explanation.walkthrough: E(ME)ER. 'Poet's' marks a poetic form.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, or emir, is an Arab title for a ruler or commander.
